sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cai was an Irish hero. He was the earliest brehon, the judge of Ireland. He belonged to the race of Milesians. His studies took him to Egypt, where he came to know the law of Moses. He arranged for Míl to marry Scota, whose parent was the Pharaoh. At the great flood, Cai escaped together with Moses. He endured the desert sojourn with him. At last he rejoined his own kin in central Europe. He then sailed from there to Ireland, where he served the invading Milesians as brehon. In Arthurian tales, the hero Kay shares this name.

okr.objective: Cai was the first brehon or judge of Ireland and a member of the Milesians.
